overviewGuide.title: Cubix: Free Cube Timer and Speedcubing Practice | Cubix
overviewGuide.heading: About Cubix
overviewGuide.description: Discover Cubix: keyboard and touch timing, supported puzzles, session statistics, offline practice and frequently asked questions.

children: Cubix is a free cube timer and algorithm trainer for desktop and mobile. No account is needed to start.
Apply the scramble, hold Space (or touch the screen), release to start, press any key to stop. Times, Ao5 and Ao12 are kept per puzzle.
F2L, OLL and PLL cases with diagrams, setups and algorithms from trusted sources. 2×2 to 7×7, Square-1, Pyraminx, Skewb, Megaminx and Clock are included.
Pick the cases you want to drill. Cubix shows a setup, times your execution and tracks your progress per case.
Best, mean, Ao5 and Ao12 with +2 and DNF handled the WCA way.
Is Cubix free? Do I need an account?
Yes, it is free. Guest practice is saved on your device. An account adds sync between devices and friends.
Once installed, the app works without a connection. Sync and messages need a connection.
Does it work on a phone?
Yes. Hold a free area of the screen to arm the timer, release to start, tap to stop.
Is this an official competition timer?
No. Cubix is a practice tool and is not affiliated with Rubik’s or the World Cube Association.
Cubix is an independent speedcubing app. Rubik’s is a trademark of its respective owner.

trainingGuide.title: How to Use the Algorithm Trainer | Cubix
trainingGuide.heading: Using the algorithm trainer
trainingGuide.description: Set up a focused algorithm training session in Cubix: select cases, apply setups, reveal solutions and review your attempts.

children: The trainer repeats the cases you choose so you can work on recognition and execution separately from full solves.
Open Cases and select the cases to practise.
Apply the setup shown on your cube.
Hold Space (or a free area of the screen), release to start, press any key to stop.
Review the session in Times. Undo removes the last time.
Start with a few cases you confuse. Keep the solution hidden to train recognition, reveal it when needed. Random U turns before the setup make recognition harder, as in a real solve.

timerGuide.title: How to Use a Rubik’s Cube Timer on Desktop & Mobile | Cubix
timerGuide.heading: Using the cube timer
timerGuide.description: Learn how to start and stop the Cubix timer with the spacebar or touchscreen, use scrambles, record penalties and review your speedcubing practice.

children: Cubix times physical solves with your keyboard or touchscreen.
The puzzle selector in the navigation bar changes the puzzle everywhere. The scramble type is chosen below the timer. New scramble generates another one.
Hold Space for 0.3 seconds until the time turns green, then release. Releasing early cancels. On a phone, hold a free area of the screen and release when ready.
Press any key or tap the screen to stop. The time is saved and the next scramble appears. Open Times to see scrambles, apply +2 or DNF, or delete a time with a right click or long press.
Standard, one-handed and blindfolded keep separate histories. Blindfolded time includes memorisation. Guest times stay on your device; sign in to sync them.

averagesGuide.heading: Ao5 and Ao12: how cube timer averages work
averagesGuide.description: Understand average of 5, average of 12, +2 penalties and DNF in Cubix. Follow worked examples and learn how averages differ from your best solve and mean.

children: Ao5 and Ao12: how cube timer averages work
A single best shows what happened once. An average shows how you usually solve. Here is how the
Take five consecutive results, drop the fastest and the slowest, average the remaining three. For 10.00, 12.00, 13.00, 14.00 and 20.00: (12 + 13 + 14) ÷ 3 =
Same idea with twelve results: drop the best and worst, average the ten left. Twelve solves from 10 to 21 seconds give an Ao12 of
A +2 adds two seconds before sorting. A DNF counts as the worst result. One DNF is dropped as the worst; two or more make the average DNF.
Best is the fastest valid result. Mean averages all valid results without dropping any. Ao5 and Ao12 use the most recent five or twelve results and stay blank until enough solves exist.
